summary: To use custom certificates on a containerized install, set the per-service inventory variables to absolute paths: gateway_tls_cert/key (plus gateway_pg_ and gateway_redis_), controller_tls_cert/key, hub_tls_cert/key, eda_tls_cert/key, postgresql_tls_cert/key and receptor_tls_cert/key; to have new ones generated, delete or move the existing files.
questions: Which inventory variables set custom TLS certificates in containerized AAP?
How do I give the containerized installer my own controller certificate?
How do I make the installer generate new certificates?

answer_card.title: Custom TLS certs (containerized)
answer_card.answer_md:
Copy the files next to the installer and set absolute paths in the inventory, for example:
```ini
gateway_tls_cert=<path>
gateway_tls_key=<path>
controller_tls_cert=<path>
controller_tls_key=<path>
hub_tls_cert=<path>
hub_tls_key=<path>
eda_tls_cert=<path>
eda_tls_key=<path>
postgresql_tls_cert=<path>
postgresql_tls_key=<path>
receptor_tls_cert=<path>
receptor_tls_key=<path>
```
Also `*_pg_tls_*` and `*_redis_tls_*` for database and Redis client certs. Then run the `install` playbook.
